papers.version_note: arXiv:2003.11151v1 (24 Mar 2020) with the Supplementary Material appended; the text layer scrambles most displayed equations.
papers.what_it_is: An experimental paper reporting an all-passive anti-PT-symmetric three-waveguide structure on thin-film lithium niobate, with thermal tuning, equal power splitting, synchronized amplitude modulation and a transition to the broken phase.

assertions.value: The authors report an all-passive realization of anti-parity-time (anti-PT) optics on a thin-film lithium niobate on insulator (LNOI) nanophotonic platform, built from three waveguides with engineered lateral coupling and loss.
quotes: In this work, we report an all-passive realization of antiPT optics on a versatile nanophotonic platform of thin-
lithium niobate on insulator (LNOI)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own platform and scope in the introduction.

assertions.value: The authors state that, before this work, anti-PT symmetry had only been realized in bulky systems or with optical gain.
quotes: Despite exciting progress, so far anti-PT symmetry has only been realized in bulky systems or with optical gain.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim about prior work with no survey in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that anti-PT effects had been observed in cold atoms, electrical circuits and, very recently, integrated photonics with balanced loss and gain induced by Brillouin scattering.
quotes: Thus far, effects of anti-PT symmetry have
been observed in cold atoms [17, 18], electrical circuits [19], and very recently integrated photonics with balanced loss and gain induced by Brillouin scattering [16].
assertions.certainty_reason: A result attributed to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that, unlike PT symmetry with real eigenvalues, anti-PT systems have purely imaginary eigenvalues, and that anti-PT can be realized without optical gain, which they describe as a source of noise or device overhead in PT systems.
quotes: Unlike PT-symmetry accompanied by real eigenvalues, anti-PT systems have purely imaginary eigenvalues
Also, anti-PT can be realized without optical gain, which has been a source of noise and/or
assertions.certainty_reason: Introductory statement attributed to cited work and author opinion.

assertions.value: The authors report that the three fully etched waveguides, in Z-cut lithium niobate bonded on silicon oxide above a silicon substrate, have measured top widths of 870, 820 and 870 nm and heights of 400 nm.
quotes: They are fully etched by ion milling on a Z-cut lithium niobate thin
The top widths of three waveguides are measured to be 870, 820 and 870 nm, respectively, and their heights are all 400 nm.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the device dimensions of its own experiment in Section 2.

assertions.value: The authors state in the Figure 1 caption that the top gap between the waveguides is around 820 nm, and that the middle trench is 1.9 micrometers wide and 690 nm thick.
quotes: The top gap between the Waveguides is around 820 nm.
The width and thickness of the middle trench are 1.9 µm and 690 nm, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated device parameters in the Figure 1 caption.

assertions.value: The authors report that the chromium strip on Waveguide 2 gives an amplitude decay rate of 1080, written with the unit dB per cm in the main text and with the unit per cm in the supplement, measured by a cut-back method; a Lumerical MODE solver simulation gives 1184 per cm.
assertions.anchor: Section 2, p.1; Supplement Section 2 and Fig. S1(c), p.2
quotes: Waveguide 2 is cladded with a chromium strip to introduce strong propagation loss, which is measured at an amplitude decay rate of 1080 dB/cm.
to be 1080/cm. It agrees with the numeric simulation result of γsim = 1184/cm using the Lumerical MODE solver.
assertions.certainty_reason: One measurement on one device.
assertions.reader_inference: The main text writes dB/cm and the supplement writes 1/cm for the same number, 1080; the units are inconsistent in the source. An amplitude decay rate in dB per cm is not the same quantity as a rate in per cm.

assertions.value: The authors state that the three-waveguide dynamics follow coupled mode equations under the slowly varying envelope approximation, with am the mode amplitude in Waveguide m, kappa the lateral coupling rate between neighboring waveguides and gamma the dissipation rate of the Waveguide 2 mode caused by the chromium strip.
quotes: The system’s wave dynamics is described by following coupled mode equations under the solwly varying envelope approximation [26]:

where am (m = 1, 2, 3) is the mode amplitude in Waveguide m. κ is the lateral coupling rate between neighboring waveguides. γ is the dissipation rate of the Waveguide 2 mode induced by the chromium strip.
assertions.certainty_reason: Definition of the model quantities in Section 2.

assertions.value: The authors define the relative propagation constants, which they call the effective detunings of the waveguide modes, as the difference of k1 and k3, and as the mean of k1 and k3 minus k2.
quotes: ∆ = k1 − k3 and ∆ = (k1 + k3)/2 − k2 are each the relative propagation constants, thus the effective detuning, of the waveguide modes.
assertions.certainty_reason: Definition given in Section 2.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer prints the second detuning with the same symbol as the first; in the original it is most likely a primed symbol. The main text and the effective Hamiltonian use the first one.

assertions.value: The authors state that, to realize an effective anti-PT system, the dissipation in Waveguide 2 must be predominantly large compared with the detuning and the coupling.
quotes: To realize an effective anti-PT system, the dissipation in Waveguide 2 must be predominantly large
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the regime of validity of its model.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer dropped the much-greater-than sign, so the exact inequality is not recoverable from the quote.

assertions.value: The authors state that the effective Hamiltonian Heff anti-commutes with the parity-time operator, which they write as a vanishing anticommutator of the PT operator and Heff, and call this an anti-PT Hamiltonian.
quotes: It anti-commutes with
{PˆTˆ , Heff} = 0.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated without derivation; the text layer scrambled the surrounding sentence.

assertions.value: The authors state that Gamma is the effective imaginary coupling strength between the two outer waveguides, which they say is distinct from typical PT systems where the coupling constants are real.
quotes: Here Γ is the effective “imaginary” coupling
ical PT systems where the coupling constants are real [27–29].
assertions.certainty_reason: A characterisation by the authors, citing other work for PT systems.

assertions.value: The authors state that when Gamma exceeds half the detuning there are two purely imaginary eigenvalues, given by minus i times Gamma plus or minus the square root of Gamma squared minus the detuning squared over four.
quotes: When Γ > ∆/2, there are two eigenvalues
which are purely imaginary.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated result without derivation in the paper; the formula itself was damaged in the text layer.

quotes: with φ = sin−1(∆/2Γ).
They are orthogonal with each other only when
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated result without derivation; the sentence about equal amplitude is split across lines in the text layer.

quotes: ∆ = 0, in which case Ψ+ experiences propagation decay at rate 2Γ, but Ψ− is lossless. Hence, only Ψ− could survive after suf

assertions.value: The authors state that the anti-PT eigenstate structure implies synchronized output and equal splitting of input power that are robust against errors in the waveguide length, loss and coupling.
quotes: The same implies synchronized
output and equal splitting of input power that are robust against
the structure’s parameter errors such as the waveguide length,
loss, and coupling.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theory-based claim by the authors, supported only by the spectrum measurement and the Fig. S5 simulation.

assertions.value: The authors state that when Gamma is below half the detuning the eigenvalues are no longer purely imaginary and the system is in a broken phase of the PT anti-symmetry, where the optical power is asymmetrically distributed over the two waveguides.
quotes: On the other hand, when Γ < ∆/2, the eignvalues are no
The system is then in a broken phase of the PT anti-symmetry, whose eigenstates are
Unlike the previous case, now the distribution of optical power is asymmetrical over the two waveguides.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated result without derivation.

assertions.value: The authors state, attributing it to Ref. 26, that in the broken phase the system exhibits nonreciprocal behaviors and the optical power mostly remains in the incident waveguide when the detuning is large.
quotes: Under this circumstance, this system exhibits nonreciprocal behaviors, and the optical power will mostly remain in the incident waveguide when ∆ is large [26].
assertions.certainty_reason: Attributed to other work and not tested here.

assertions.value: The authors state that two microheaters 1.5 micrometers above Waveguides 1 and 3 tune the detuning through the thermo-optic effect with negligible loss, that fundamental TM modes are used in all waveguides for the highest thermo-optic coefficient of LNOI, and that a trench above the center waveguide partially blocks thermal flow.
quotes: two microheaters are deposited 1.5 µm above Waveguide 1 and 3, respectively, to precisely tune ∆ via thermooptic effects while inducing only negligible loss.
fundamental transverse-magnetic (TM) modes are employed for all waveguides
a trench is also etched above the center waveguide to partially block thermal
assertions.certainty_reason: Design of the paper's own device stated in Section 2.

assertions.value: The authors report that with a maximum of 200 mW electric power applied to either microheater, they can sweep the detuning and observe the transition between the symmetry phase and the broken phase, in both directions.
quotes: With a maximum of 200 mW electric power applied to either microheater, we are able to sweep ∆ and observe the phase transition from the symmetry to broken phase, and vice versa
assertions.certainty_reason: One device, one set of sweeps.

assertions.value: The authors report that a polarized beam at 1550 nm is coupled through an objective lens into the fundamental TM mode of Waveguide 3, the output from either outer waveguide is collected by a lensed fiber and measured with a power meter, and the input power is 10 dBm.
assertions.anchor: Section 3, p.3; Supplement Fig. S2 and text, p.3
quotes: a polarized beam at 1550 nm is coupled into a fundamental TM mode of Waveguide 3
nm and the input power is 10 dBm.
assertions.certainty_reason: Setup of the paper's own experiment.

assertions.value: The authors report that the total coupling loss of reference waveguides on the same wafer is typically measured to be around minus 14 dB.
quotes: The total coupling loss of reference waveguides on the same wafer
is typcially measured to be around -14 dB.
assertions.certainty_reason: A typical value from reference structures on one wafer.

assertions.value: The authors report that increasing heating power on the microheater above Waveguide 1 raised the output of both waveguides, with both maximized at 135 mW, where the detuning is close to zero, and that after switching to the heater on the other outer waveguide the output from Waveguide 1 was minimized at 201 mW.
quotes: As the applied heating power reaches 135 mW, the output optical power from the two waveguides is maximized simultaneously.
The output power from Waveguide 1 is minimized when the heating power reaches 201 mW.
assertions.certainty_reason: One measurement on one device.

assertions.value: The authors report in the supplement that the effective detuning extracted from the output power measurements reaches zero at a heating power of 144 mW.
quotes: In Fig. S4(b), the effective detuning reaches zero when the heating power is 144 mW.
assertions.certainty_reason: One extraction from one device.
assertions.reader_inference: The main text puts the output maximum at 135 mW with the detuning close to zero, and the supplement puts the zero at 144 mW. The paper does not reconcile the two.

assertions.value: The authors report an overall coupling efficiency of minus 14.8 dB, extracted by fitting the heating-sweep data, equal to an average value of 0.033, and used for both waveguides.
quotes: is extract to be -14.8 dB by
Thus in the main text, we choose their average value of 0.033, or -14.8 dB, as the coupling
assertions.certainty_reason: A fitted value from one device.

assertions.value: The authors report in Table S1 the fitting parameters of Gamma, the baseline detuning, the detuning slope with heating power and the two coupling efficiencies in dB, listed as 20.96, 32.95, 0.21, minus 15.23 and minus 14.24.
assertions.certainty_reason: Fitted values from one device.
assertions.reader_inference: Gamma is 20.96 per cm here, while the Fig. 4 simulation uses a Gamma of 17 per cm. The paper does not explain the difference.

assertions.value: The authors report an average inter-waveguide coupling strength kappa of 136 per cm, extracted from the output power measurements and used for the theoretical eigenvalue curves, with a detuning slope of 0.22 per cm per mW.
assertions.anchor: Section 3, Fig. 3, p.3; Supplement Fig. S4, p.3
quotes: the theoretical results using κ = 136 cm−1, obtained by averaging over the various heating power applied, and d∆/dp = 0.22 cm−1mW−1
From Fig. S4(a), the average coupling strength is κ = 136/cm
assertions.certainty_reason: A value extracted from one device.

assertions.value: The authors report that the extracted kappa is nearly independent of the applied heating power, while the detuning increases linearly with it.
assertions.anchor: Section 3, Figs. S3 and S4, p.3
quotes: As expected, κ is nearly independent of the applied heating power, while ∆ increases linearly with it, as shown in Fig. S3 and S4 of Supplementary Material.
assertions.certainty_reason: One device.

assertions.value: The authors report a linear-fit thermo-optic detuning coefficient of 22.4 times ten to the power minus two per mW per cm, close to the single-waveguide value of Eq. S6, and say this shows that the trench is effective in stopping thermal flow to the other waveguide.
quotes: which is close to that obtained for the single waveguide case in
This result shows that the trench is effective in stopping the thermal
assertions.certainty_reason: One device, one fit.

assertions.value: The authors report that a Mach-Zehnder interferometer with a microheater in one arm was used to calibrate the thermo-optic shift of the propagation constant, which they state is linearly proportional to the heating power, recorded from 0 mW to 192 mW.
assertions.anchor: Supplement, Fig. S1(a)-(b) and Eq. (S6), p.2
quotes: The shift in the wave propagation constant k caused by the thermo-optic effect is linearly proportional to the heating power P.
The output power of the interferometer is recorded as P is varied gradually from 0 mW to 192 mW.
assertions.certainty_reason: One calibration on one device.

assertions.value: The authors report a clear phase transition at the exceptional point where Gamma equals half the detuning, as predicted by Eqs. (4) and (6), with the experimental eigenvalues extracted from the measured powers compared with theory.
quotes: As shown, there is a clear phase transition occurring at the exceptional point of Γ = ∆/2, as predicted by Eqs.(4) and (6).
assertions.certainty_reason: An experimental result from one device.

assertions.value: The authors report that in the anti-PT phase the two purely imaginary eigenvalues have an amplitude difference that increases to nearly 30 per cm as the detuning is decreased to 0.6 Gamma, while the real wave vectors of the two eigenmodes remain the same.
quotes: whose amplitude difference increases to nearly 30/cm as the detuning is decreased to ∆ = 0.6Γ.
Meanwhile, the real wave vectors for the two eignmodes remain the same.
assertions.certainty_reason: Values read from one device.

assertions.value: The authors state that in the broken phase the two eigenstates share the same dissipation rate but have different wave vectors.
quotes: When Γ < ∆/2, in contrast, the two eigenstates share the same dissipation rate but have different wave vectors.
assertions.certainty_reason: Experimental and theoretical statement of the paper.

assertions.value: The authors report that with 135 mW heating power on Waveguide 1, the outputs of the two outer waveguides were measured while the wavelength was swept over a 130 nm range, set by the laser tuning range, and showed equal power splitting with less than plus or minus 0.05 dB deviation.
quotes: Waveguide 1 is applied with 135 mW heating power to bring the effective detuning close to zero.
the input laser wavelength is swept over a spectral range of 130 nm, as allowed by our laser tuning range.
equal power splitting is observed over the entire spectrum, with less than ±0.05dB deviation.
assertions.certainty_reason: One device, one measurement.

assertions.value: The authors state that equal beam splitting under anti-PT symmetry, unlike directional coupling, is not sensitive to the inter-waveguide coupling strength, the waveguide length, its propagation loss or the optical wavelength.
quotes: Distinct to directional coupling [30], such equal beam splitting realized under anti-PT symmetry is not sensitive to the inter-waveguide coupling strength, the waveguide length, its propagation loss, or the optical wavelength.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; only the wavelength insensitivity was measured.

assertions.value: The authors state that equal splitting only requires a condition relating Gamma to the detuning and to the inverse waveguide length, which they say greatly boosts the tolerance of nanofabrication errors compared with a coherent-optical circuit.
quotes: As such equal splitting only requires Γ ∆, 1/L (L is the waveguide length)
it greatly boosts the tolerance of nanofabrication errors as compared with a coherent-optical circuit
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim backed by one simulation of a Hermitian structure.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer dropped the much-greater-than sign between Gamma and the detuning in the quote.

assertions.value: The authors state that the operational bandwidth is much wider than typically achievable with beam-splitters based on multimode interference or directional coupling.
quotes: Furthermore, this operational bandwidth is much wider than typically achievable with beam-splitters based on multimode interference or directional coupling [31].
assertions.certainty_reason: No comparison data in the paper; the 130 nm sweep was limited by the laser.

assertions.value: The authors report a simulation of a Hermitian structure of the same three waveguides without the metal strip, with the top gap varied from 810 nm to 910 nm, in which the outputs are quite sensitive to the gap and a 3-dB tolerance in power splitting would require the fabrication error to be less than 10 nm.
quotes: The top gap of the neighboring waveguides is gradually increased from 810 nm to 910 nm.
where the waveguide outputs are quite sensitive to the top gap. A 3-dB tolerance in power splitting would require the fabrication error to be less than 10 nm.
assertions.certainty_reason: One simulation.

assertions.value: The authors state that with two inputs of equal amplitude the output powers of the two waveguides are always equal regardless of the relative input phase, in both the anti-PT symmetry phase and the broken phase, while the total output power is not conserved and depends on the relative phase.
quotes: with two inputs of equal amplitude, the output power of the two waveguides is always equal, regardless of the relative phase between the two inputs.
This holds irrespective of whether the system is in the anti-PT symmetry or its broken phase.
the total output power is not conserved and sensitive to the relative phase.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated from theory and the Fig. 4 data from one device.

assertions.value: The authors state that this behavior contrasts with coherent-optical couplers described by Hermitian Hamiltonians, where the total output power is conserved but its distribution over the outputs depends on the input relative phase.
quotes: where the total output power is conserved but its distribution over the outputs is sensitive to the input relative phase.
assertions.certainty_reason: A general statement about conventional couplers with no data in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors report an imbalanced Mach-Zehnder circuit with a 435 micrometer path difference, in which scanning the wavelength from 1544 nm to 1550 nm sweeps the input relative phase theta over 16 radians, nearly linearly with wavelength.
quotes: In our structure, dL = 435 µm, so that by scanning λ from 1544 nm to 1550 nm, θ is swept over 16 radians nearly linearly with λ.
Their relative phase acquired before the anti-PT structure is given by θ = ndL/λ
assertions.certainty_reason: Setup of the paper's own experiment.
assertions.reader_inference: The relation as printed omits a factor of two pi; the quoted numbers are consistent with a phase of two pi times n dL over lambda.

assertions.value: The authors report that in all measured cases the two outputs are equal in power except for a constant factor of about 2 dB, which they attribute to loss differences such as nanofabrication stitching errors, and that the total output oscillates with theta, reaching 15 dB extinction at 185 mW heating power on Waveguide 1.
quotes: As seen, in all cases, the two outputs are always equal in power except for a constant factor (∼ 2 dB), which is likely attributed to the difference in the waveguide propagation and coupling loss in the two outputs
where a high 15 dB extinction is achieved with 185 mW heating power applied to the microheater above Waveguide 1, as seen in Fig. 4(b).
assertions.certainty_reason: Measurements from one device.

assertions.value: The authors report that the Fig. 4 simulation uses the Hamiltonian with Gamma of 17 per cm and other parameters from the earlier measurements, with baseline detuning as the only fitting parameter, fitted to 22 per cm at 185 mW, and with the detuning at other heater settings computed from its linear dependence on heating power.
quotes: we simulate the system dynamics using Hamiltonian (3), with Γ = 17 cm−1, the coupling
to be 22 cm−1 when the heating power is 185 mW, as shown in 4(f).
For other heating settings, ∆ is calculated directly using its linear dependence of the applied heating power.
assertions.certainty_reason: Fit on one device.
assertions.reader_inference: Gamma of 17 per cm differs from the 20.96 per cm in Table S1; the paper does not explain the difference.

assertions.value: The authors state that the baseline detuning is the only fitting parameter in the phase-sweep comparison because it is extremely sensitive to the waveguide cross section and cannot otherwise be determined.
quotes: as it is extremely sensitive to the waveguide’s cross section and cannot be otherwise determined.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit of its own analysis in Section 3.

assertions.value: The authors report that in all cases the experimental and simulated output power agree fairly well.
quotes: As shown, in all cases, the experimental and simulation results agree fairly well.
assertions.certainty_reason: Qualitative agreement on one device; no fit metric given.

assertions.value: The authors report that at a detuning over twice Gamma of 0.65, in the anti-PT symmetry phase, the output power experiences the strongest loss when the two inputs are in phase and the least loss when they are out of phase.
quotes: In Fig. 4(f), ∆/2Γ = 0.65, so that the system is in anti-PT symmetry.
The output power thus experiences the strongest loss when the two inputs are in phase and the least loss when they are out of phase.
assertions.certainty_reason: Result from one device.

assertions.value: The authors report that as the detuning increases the loss difference between the two input-phase cases decreases and so does the extinction, which drops to 5 dB in Fig. 4(i) at a detuning over twice Gamma of 1.85, in the broken phase.
quotes: As ∆ increases, the propagation loss difference in the two cases decreases, so is the extinction.
In Fig. 4(i), when ∆/2Γ = 1.85, the system is
broken phase, for which the extinction drops to 5 dB.
assertions.certainty_reason: Result from one device.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that they observed anti-PT symmetry and its transition into a broken phase on an all-passive nanophotonic platform, with equal power splitting, synchronized amplitude modulation and phase-controlled dissipation by thermal tuning.
quotes: In conclusion, We have observed anti-PT symmetry and its transition into a broken phase using an all-passive, nanophotonic platform.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' conclusion from a single device.

assertions.value: The authors suggest the structure could be used to construct synchronized modulators, novel optical interferometers and nontrivial logical gates such as an exclusive-OR phase gate, and that electronic tuning of the relative phase might give electro-optical interfaces.
quotes: They could be used to construct synchronized modulators, novel optical interferometers, and nontrivial logical gates, such as exclusive-OR phase gate.
By replacing the thermal tuning with electronic tuning to control the relative phase, one might also realize exotic electro-optical interfaces as well.
assertions.certainty_reason: Prospective applications with no data.
